records.region: Nevada–California interior: western Palmetto Mountains, Palmetto Wash, Fish Lake Valley and Columbus Salt Marsh.
records.naming_scope_hold_reason: The two bounded hydronyms do not establish a representative name for the entire selected combination of wash, valley drainage, marsh/playa and interbasin spillway. The hold is not based merely on multiple reach labels.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Palmetto Wash labels the southern canyon wash; McAfee Creek labels a bounded central receiving reach. The selection also includes an unnamed opening and axial intervals, Fish Lake Valley Marsh, The Gap and Columbus Salt Marsh. Those wetland, playa and geographic passage names are kept separate.
records.completion_scope: Every stored part is covered by actual original geographic material, including the opening, canyon joins, alluvial transition, receiving tributary/wetland passages, northern playa, The Gap, outlet fan and actual terminal. Report58 independently supports the geographic overflow connection. No material selected through-link remains unestablished.
records.supported_name_scope: Palmetto Wash labels the southern canyon wash; McAfee Creek labels a bounded central receiving reach. The selection also includes an unnamed opening and axial intervals, Fish Lake Valley Marsh, The Gap and Columbus Salt Marsh. Those wetland, playa and geographic passage names are kept separate.

scope_limits: The two bounded hydronyms do not establish a representative name for the entire selected combination of wash, valley drainage, marsh/playa and interbasin spillway. The hold is not based merely on multiple reach labels.
Exact hydronym-change vertices, individual marsh threads, current irrigation routing, water levels and overflow frequency are outside the naming task.
The initial tributary and several axial intervals remain unnamed in the inspected sources. Formal naming-registry status is unverified.

records.region: Sierra de Santa Cruz–Chahal/Livingston–Gracias a Dios–Sarstún coast
records.material_pending_reason: FID10579 initial Sechalcate/Chacalté-side opening through Secar–Secoyoute to the Semanzana-side valley is not established by the inspected cartography and imagery. The remaining Sarstún corridor, other three fragments and actual coastal terminal are supported; additional broad downstream naming references would not resolve this specific gap.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Sarstún lower river and receiving coastal system supported. Semanzana and Gracias a Dios are bounded upper/intermediate reach names, with Chahal/Chiyú confluence context. Unestablished initial Sierra de Santa Cruz transfer prevents completed whole-selected-system representative identity.
records.completion_scope: All four fragments considered. Western/northern river, intermediate joins, generalized middle/lower corridor, sidewater/wetland setting and actual coast terminal have ordinary-scale correspondence. Initial opening and southern Secar–Secoyoute drainage transfer remain unestablished. One material-pending state only.
records.supported_name_scope: Sarstún lower river and receiving coastal system supported. Semanzana and Gracias a Dios are bounded upper/intermediate reach names, with Chahal/Chiyú confluence context. Unestablished initial Sierra de Santa Cruz transfer prevents completed whole-selected-system representative identity.

scope_limits: Initial Sechalcate/Chacalté-side headwaters to Semanzana-side valley transfer unestablished. No assertion that this passage is impossible or lacks a local name.
Reach names are not forced across all fragments; no exact legal name boundary assigned.
No selected tributary fragment exists. Unselected joining rivers and sidewater bodies are distinguished.
No reservoir or managed-water passage established; roads, cultivation and settlement are geographic setting only.
Laguna Grande vicinity is a river/wetland receiving setting, not proof of lagoon-center traversal or present exchange.
Exact historic/project restrictions remain preserved without a nationwide or agency-wide ban.

records.region: Southwestern Alaska; upper Goodnews River, Goodnews Lake and Goodnews Bay
records.geographic_disambiguation: Representative identity of the selected upper Goodnews River–Goodnews Lake–lower Goodnews River corridor and its coastal receiving setting. The chosen headward feeder, lake passage and terminal shore extension are included as connected components; no scalar river name is assigned to every position, lake or bay. North Fork is a documented descriptive designation for the main Goodnews River, not a separately verified registry alias.
records.completion_scope: Completed bounded representative-system correspondence across all selected parts, including the chosen opening, river and lake links, ordinary tributary joins, wetland-estuary passage and actual terminal. No real unsupported intercomponent link remains within this scope. This is research-only identity support, with no product naming change or accepted scalar name.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the selected upper Goodnews River–Goodnews Lake–lower Goodnews River corridor and its coastal receiving setting. The chosen headward feeder, lake passage and terminal shore extension are included as connected components; no scalar river name is assigned to every position, lake or bay. North Fork is a documented descriptive designation for the main Goodnews River, not a separately verified registry alias.

scope_limits: The chosen upstream opening is a modeled start on a mapped feeder; the ultimate natural source and exact beginning of the Goodnews scalar name are not assigned.
Goodnews Lake, the smaller outlet waterbody and Goodnews Bay retain separate component identities. A single river scalar is not applied across lake or coastal water.
The final rendered extension and source endpoint differ within the same estuary and shore receiving setting. No exact current shoreline, bank or active distributary is selected.
North Fork is supported as a descriptive designation in the read report; formal aliases and registry status remain unverified.
No selected glacial or managed-transfer segment is depicted by the read cartography. This does not assert a hydrological inventory of every feature in the basin.

records.region: Northern contributing valleys, San Ignacio oasis and the eastern Laguna San Ignacio receiving plain, Mulegé, Baja California Sur, Mexico.
records.geographic_disambiguation: San Ignacio is directly supported for the receiving corridor through the oasis and toward Laguna San Ignacio, and is a representative connected-system identity. This does not name every northern feeder, oasis pool, dry-plain thread or the lagoon itself. The northern Santa Martha map label and the study prose’s Santa María form remain source-specific observations rather than unverified aliases.
records.completion_scope: The full chosen opening and all twenty stored parts and joins were matched at ordinary corridor scale using the retained independent cartographic originals and four overlapping photographic views. The oasis, local road/crossing features, lower dry wash, broad alluvial/tidal receiving plain and actual lagoon-margin terminal are accounted for. The supported representative San Ignacio identity coexists with distinct or unnamed contributing reaches; no whole-object scalar name is accepted.
records.supported_name_scope: San Ignacio is directly supported for the receiving corridor through the oasis and toward Laguna San Ignacio, and is a representative connected-system identity. This does not name every northern feeder, oasis pool, dry-plain thread or the lagoon itself. The northern Santa Martha map label and the study prose’s Santa María form remain source-specific observations rather than unverified aliases.

scope_limits: Formal registry identity and Korean standardized naming are unverified. The finding supplies a supported representative system candidate only.
Neither the northern chosen opening nor every separate upper reach is assigned the San Ignacio name. Santa Martha and Santa María source forms are not asserted to be official synonyms.

The seasonal wash, vegetated oasis and tidal receiving plain do not imply continuously wetted or permanently free-flowing conditions. Local crossings and waterbody appearance are geographic observations, not engineering or operating-state findings.
The final lagoon-side display continuation is supported at ordinary receiving-setting scale, without claiming that the generalized line follows one exact modern channel across the flat.
All source originals are historical or mosaic-based; source lengths, principal headwaters and generalized marine attributes are not transferred to the pinned selection as surveyed facts.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
